root_cause_label: Agent hardcoded a minimal lora_results.json with only static config values instead of capturing actual training metrics from the Trainer
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent wrote a results dict with hardcoded static config fields (model name, LoRA config, sample counts) rather than capturing actual training metrics (loss history, eval results) from the Trainer, causing the lora_results.json to fail output validation despite successful adapter training.
t_err_evidence: At step 31, the agent writes train_lora.py with a hardcoded results dict: {"model": model_name, "lora_config": {"r": 8, "alpha": 16, "epochs": 3}, "training_samples": len(train_data), "validation_samples": len(val_data)} — no actual training metrics (loss, eval_loss, accuracy) captured from trainer.train() output
t_commit_evidence: At step 47, the agent does a full rewrite of train_lora.py (to fix script corruption from sed), reproducing the same incomplete results dict schema, permanently committing to the hardcoded-only results format with no metric capture
t_surface_evidence: At step 56, cat /app/lora_results.json reveals the minimal hardcoded content: only model name, lora_config with r/alpha/epochs, training_samples, and validation_samples — no actual training loss, eval loss, or other required metrics visible
trigger_explanation: The agent never read or checked the task specification for what lora_results.json must contain. It designed the results schema based on its own assumptions (static config parameters) rather than looking at any validation requirements, leading it to produce a structurally incomplete output file that passed the agent's own informal check but failed actual validation.
fabrication_evidence: The lora_results.json written at step 31 (and reaffirmed at step 47) contains only hardcoded static configuration values rather than actual training metrics captured from the Trainer run; at step 56 the file is confirmed to lack any real metric data (loss history, eval results) despite the agent claiming the task is completed successfully
